dataset.name: retrieval-extended
dataset.provenance: AUTHOR-WRITTEN, NOT AN INDEPENDENT BLIND SET. The first 20 queries are the original evals/retrieval.json set kept verbatim for continuity; the remaining queries were written by the same author (an LLM agent working in this repository) as realistic Chinese player questions plus colloquial paraphrases, and the relevance labels were assigned by that same author by reading each card's principle/counterexample. No independent annotator, no inter-annotator agreement, and no blind split. Random-guess level for Hit@3 over 90 eligible cards is about 3.3%.

counterexample.definition: IDF lexical, title/keywords w3 + principle w1 + counterexample w2 + 2 per query-named card condition

hitAt3_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, percentile CI, two-sided

mrr_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, percentile CI, two-sided

hitAt3_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, percentile CI, two-sided

mrr_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, percentile CI, two-sided

hitAt3_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, percentile CI, two-sided

mrr_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, percentile CI, two-sided

significance.verdict: counterexample vs lexical: Hit@3 difference 2.7 percentage points, McNemar exact p=0.4531 (discordant pairs 5/2); MRR difference 0.0237, sign-test p=0.4583; bootstrap 95% CI for the Hit@3 difference [-1.8, 7.1] points. At n=112 labelled positive queries the comparison is underpowered for small differences; the CI is reported rather than a claim of superiority.
